Definition: from G2685; to be a sentinel, i.e. to inspect insidiously:--spy out.
BiblicalUsage: False brethren came in privily to spy out our liberty in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe liberty is spied on before it is stolen, and the church must watch for the spies.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
